faqs.question: What is the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.answer: A roughly 12-15 day trek through the Khumbu to the foot of Everest, topping out around 5,364 m (17,598 ft).

faqs.question: What is the best time to trek to Everest Base Camp?
faqs.answer: Spring (Mar-May) and autumn (Sep-Nov); winter is very cold and the Jun-Aug monsoon is wet.

faqs.question: What level of fitness is required for the trek?
faqs.answer: Moderate fitness; prepare with hiking or cardio for long days on rough ground.

faqs.question: How do I prepare for the trek?
faqs.answer: Train, get proper boots, warm clothing and a high-altitude sleeping bag, and learn altitude-sickness signs and hydration habits.

faqs.question: Do I need a guide and porter?
faqs.answer: Independent trekking is possible but a guide and porter are strongly recommended; the porter carries your gear.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodation can I expect?
faqs.answer: Teahouses with shared, usually twin, rooms; most serve meals.

faqs.question: Is it safe to trek in the Everest region?
faqs.answer: Generally yes with a reputable company; guides are first-aid trained and manage weather and acclimatization.

faqs.question: What permits do I need for the trek?
faqs.answer: TIMS card and Sagarmatha National Park permit; the company arranges both.

faqs.question: How can I stay connected during the trek?
faqs.answer: Limited: paid Wi-Fi at some teahouses; a local SIM works intermittently higher up.

faqs.question: What is the cost of the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.answer: Package covers lodging, meals, guide/porter, permits and transport; US$1,120 pp for 2-4 people vs US$1,305 solo.

faqs.question: What is the Everest Base Camp Trek via Jiri?
faqs.answer: An alternative route starting at Jiri (~190 km east of Kathmandu) with a gentler climb through the Solu region.

faqs.question: Why choose the Jiri route?
faqs.answer: Fewer crowds than the Lukla route, traditional villages, green hills and more cultural immersion.

faqs.question: How long does the trek take?
faqs.answer: About 16-20 days depending on itinerary and pace.

faqs.question: What is the best time to trek via Jiri?
faqs.answer: Spring (Mar-May) and autumn (Sep-Nov) for stable weather and clear views.

faqs.question: What level of fitness is required?
faqs.answer: Moderate; long days and steep sections, so hiking and cardio training are advised.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodation can I expect?
faqs.answer: Basic teahouses with shared rooms and warm meals.

faqs.question: Do I need a guide and porter?
faqs.answer: Possible without, but strongly recommended for safety and convenience.

faqs.question: What permits do I need?
faqs.answer: TIMS card and Sagarmatha National Park permit; the company helps arrange them.

faqs.question: How can I stay connected?
faqs.answer: Paid Wi-Fi at some teahouses; local SIM gives patchy service in lower areas.

faqs.question: What is the cost of the trek?
faqs.answer: Varies by itinerary; covers lodging, meals, guide/porter, permits and transport. US$1,780 pp for 2-4 people.

faqs.question: What is the Everest Panorama Trek?
faqs.answer: A popular Khumbu route with Everest views without a full high-altitude push; usually 7-10 days.

faqs.question: What is the best time to trek?
faqs.answer: Spring (Mar-May) and autumn (Sep-Nov); winter brings snow and the Jun-Aug monsoon brings rain and cloud.

faqs.question: What level of fitness is required?
faqs.answer: Moderate; several hours of walking daily on steep trails. Train with hiking, cardio and strength work.

faqs.question: How do I get to the starting point of the trek?
faqs.answer: Short domestic flight Kathmandu-Lukla; allow spare days for weather delays.

faqs.question: What permits are needed?
faqs.answer: Sagarmatha National Park permit, and possibly a TIMS card; the agency confirms and arranges.

faqs.question: What accommodations can I expect?
faqs.answer: Basic teahouses, usually twin rooms, some with attached bathroom, shared dining rooms.

faqs.question: What about altitude sickness?
faqs.answer: Gradual ascent helps; hydrate, go slowly, watch for headache, nausea or dizziness and descend if needed.

faqs.question: Do I need a guide or can I trek independently?
faqs.answer: Possible alone, but a guide is strongly recommended for safety, navigation and permits.

faqs.question: What should I pack for the trek?
faqs.answer: Sturdy boots, warm layers, sleeping bag, backpack, poles, first-aid kit, water purification, camera, toiletries.

faqs.question: What is the Gokyo Chola & Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.answer: A Khumbu route linking Gokyo Lakes, the Cho La pass and Everest Base Camp; typically 16-20 days.

faqs.question: What is the best time to do this trek?
faqs.answer: Spring (Mar-May) and autumn (Sep-Nov); monsoon and winter bring rain, snow and cold.

faqs.question: What level of fitness is required?
faqs.answer: Challenging, with long high-altitude days; cardio, strength training and practice hikes recommended.

faqs.question: How do I get to the starting point of the trek?
faqs.answer: Fly Kathmandu-Lukla (weather can delay flights), then walk toward Namche.

faqs.question: What permits are required for this trek?
faqs.answer: Sagarmatha National Park permit and TIMS card, arranged by an agency or in Kathmandu.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodations can I expect?
faqs.answer: Basic teahouses, mostly shared rooms, communal dining with local and international food.

faqs.question: How do I deal with altitude sickness?
faqs.answer: Acclimatize gradually, hydrate, watch for headache/nausea/fatigue and descend if severe.

faqs.question: Should I hire a guide or trek independently?
faqs.answer: A guide is strongly recommended, especially for the Cho La pass.

faqs.question: What should I pack for the trek?
faqs.answer: Boots, layers, warm sleeping bag, backpack, poles, first-aid kit, water purification, sunscreen, toiletries.

faqs.question: What is the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.answer: A popular route to the base of Annapurna with views of Annapurna I, Annapurna South and Machapuchare; usually 10-14 days.

faqs.question: What is the best time to trek to Annapurna Base Camp?
faqs.answer: Mar-May (rhododendrons) and Sep-Nov (clear air).

faqs.question: Do I need a permit to trek to Annapurna Base Camp?
faqs.answer: Yes: ACAP and TIMS card, from Pokhara or Kathmandu.

faqs.question: What is the level of difficulty for the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.answer: Moderate to challenging; base camp ~4,130 m (13,550 ft) with long, steep days.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodation can I expect?
faqs.answer: Teahouses with beds, meals and shared bathrooms; more basic higher up.

faqs.question: What should I pack for the trek?
faqs.answer: Warm sleeping bag, boots, layers, waterproof jacket, poles, first-aid kit, snacks, bottle, purification tablets.

faqs.question: Is it safe to trek to Annapurna Base Camp?
faqs.answer: Generally safe; altitude sickness is the main risk, managed by acclimatization and a guide.

faqs.question: Can I trek solo, or do I need a guide?
faqs.answer: Solo is possible; a guide is strongly recommended for first-timers.

faqs.question: How physically fit do I need to be?
faqs.answer: Moderate fitness; cardio, leg strength and hill training beforehand.

faqs.question: What kind of food can I expect during the trek?
faqs.answer: Dal bhat, noodle soup, curries, some Western dishes; teahouses can meet dietary needs if told in advance.

faqs.question: What is the Langtang Valley and Gosaikunda Trek?
faqs.answer: A Langtang National Park trek through the valley to the Gosaikunda Lakes and Tamang/Sherpa villages; 10-15 days.

faqs.question: When is the best time to trek?
faqs.answer: Spring (Mar-May) and autumn (Sep-Nov); winter is snowy and monsoon makes trails muddy.

faqs.question: What level of fitness is required?
faqs.answer: Moderate to challenging; build endurance with hiking, cardio and strength training.

faqs.question: How do I reach the starting point of the trek?
faqs.answer: Drive Kathmandu-Syabrubesi, about 7-8 hours.

faqs.question: What permits do I need?
faqs.answer: Langtang National Park permit and TIMS card, from Kathmandu or via an agency.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodations can I expect?
faqs.answer: Teahouses with mostly shared rooms and communal dining; basic but comfortable.

faqs.question: How do I manage altitude sickness?
faqs.answer: Ascend gradually, hydrate, watch symptoms, descend and tell your guide if severe.

faqs.question: Is it necessary to hire a guide?
faqs.answer: Not required but strongly recommended for safety, navigation, permits and culture.

faqs.question: What should I pack for the trek?
faqs.answer: Boots, warm layers, sleeping bag, backpack, poles, first-aid kit, purification tablets, sunscreen.

faqs.question: What are the key highlights of the Helambu Valley Trek?

faqs.question: Are there accommodations available along the trek?

faqs.question: What kind of food can I expect on the trek?

faqs.question: What are the key highlights of the Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.answer: Walled Lo Manthang, rock formations, caves, monasteries, Dhaulagiri and Annapurna views.

faqs.question: What is the Manaslu Round Trek?
faqs.answer: A circuit around Manaslu (world's 8th-highest) in Gorkha District, usually 13-16 days.

faqs.question: What is the best time to trek in Manaslu?
faqs.answer: Spring and autumn; winter snow and monsoon landslide risk.

faqs.question: What is the difficulty level of the trek?
faqs.answer: Moderate to challenging, crossing Larkya La at 5,160 m (~16,930 ft).

faqs.question: What permits do I need for the trek?
faqs.answer: Special Manaslu permit (costlier) plus TIMS card, via a registered agency.

faqs.question: What should I pack for the trek?
faqs.answer: Boots, layers, sleeping bag, waterproof jacket, sun protection, first-aid kit, refillable bottle.

faqs.question: Are there accommodations available along the trek?
faqs.answer: Basic teahouses with food and beds; book ahead in peak season.

faqs.question: What kind of food can I expect on the trek?
faqs.answer: Dal bhat, momo, thukpa; few Western options in remote areas.

faqs.question: Is it necessary to hire a guide for the trek?
faqs.answer: Not required but strongly recommended; porters available.

faqs.question: What are the key highlights of the Manaslu Round Trek?
faqs.answer: Manaslu views, Samagaon village, Larkya La, monasteries and wildlife.

faqs.question: What is the Manaslu Tsum Valley Trek?
faqs.answer: Combines Manaslu views with the Tibetan-influenced Tsum Valley; usually 16-20 days.

faqs.question: What is the best time to trek in Manaslu Tsum Valley?
faqs.answer: Spring and autumn; monsoon landslides and winter snow.

faqs.question: What is the difficulty level of the trek?
faqs.answer: Moderate to challenging, with Larkya La at 5,160 m (16,930 ft).

faqs.question: What permits do I need for the trek?
faqs.answer: Manaslu special permit and TIMS card, plus a separate Tsum Valley permit, via a registered agency.

faqs.question: What should I pack for the trek?
faqs.answer: Boots, layers, sleeping bag, waterproof jacket, sun protection, first-aid kit, refillable bottle.

faqs.question: Are there accommodations available along the trek?
faqs.answer: Basic teahouses with meals; book ahead in peak season.

faqs.question: What kind of food can I expect on the trek?
faqs.answer: Dal bhat, momo, thukpa; limited Western options.

faqs.question: Is it necessary to hire a guide for the trek?
faqs.answer: Not mandatory but strongly recommended; porters available.

faqs.question: What are the key highlights of the Manaslu Tsum Valley Trek?
faqs.answer: Manaslu views, Tsum Valley, Rachen and Mu Gompa, local Tsum culture.
